name: Loose and Conversational
prompt: Favor natural speech rhythm, selective end rhymes, and emotional clarity.

name: Balanced
prompt: Use consistent end rhymes with occasional internal patterns while keeping every line understandable.

name: Dense Multisyllabic
prompt: Use dense multisyllabic schemes, internal chains, slant rhymes, and controlled enjambment without sounding mechanical.

name: Technical Maximum
prompt: Use highly technical rhyme webs, recurring vowel families, rapid internal echoes, and clean performability.

name: Hook Simple / Verses Dense
prompt: Keep the chorus simple and immediate while the verses carry dense internal and multisyllabic patterns.

name: None / Free Verse
prompt: Use free verse with natural speech stress and imagery instead of a regular end-rhyme scheme.

name: Sparse End Rhyme
prompt: Rhyme only selected line endings so the lyric stays conversational and emotionally clear.

name: Simple Couplets
prompt: Use easy-to-follow paired end rhymes with clean stresses and no dense internal technique.

name: Pop Regular
prompt: Use a predictable radio-friendly rhyme pattern with simple verses and highly repeatable chorus wording.

name: Internal Accents
prompt: Keep end rhymes light but place short internal echoes and vowel matches inside important lines.

name: Technical Dense
prompt: Use frequent multisyllabic internals slant rhymes and cross-line patterns while preserving clear delivery.

name: Maximum Rhyme Chains
prompt: Carry connected multisyllabic vowel families across several consecutive lines with precise performable rhythm.

name: Variable by Section
prompt: Use loose conversational rhyming in setup sections denser rhyme work in verses and simple repetition in hooks.

name: Melodic Repetition
prompt: Let repeated melodic phrases and key words provide cohesion instead of forcing dense end rhymes.
